title: Positive degree implies ample
statement:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve of
genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ and
$\mathcal L$ a line bundle with $\deg\mathcal L>0$
([def-sc-pic0]). Then $\mathcal L$ is
ample.

proof.text: Let $m\geq1$. The $m$-fold tensor product $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module and its class in the Picard group is $[\mathcal L^{\otimes m}]=m[\mathcal L]$, because the group law of $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is induced by $\otimes$ ([def-sc-picard-group], [lem-sc-pic-group]); induction on $m$, using $\mathcal L^{\otimes(m+1)}=\mathcal L^{\otimes m}\otimes\mathcal L$. By [def-sc-pic0] the degree $\deg:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\mathbf Z$ is a group homomorphism (the divisor degree, well defined by [lem-sc-deg-principal-zero], transported along the identification $\operatorname{Cl}(C)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ of abelian groups that [def-sc-pic0] names in its statement), so $\deg(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})=\deg(m[\mathcal L])=m\deg\mathcal L$.

proof.text: Put $m:=2g+1$, where $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\geq0$ is the genus ([def-sc-genus]); then $m\geq1$. Since $\deg\mathcal L$ is an integer with $\deg\mathcal L>0$, $\deg\mathcal L\geq1$, and by step 1 $\deg(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})=(2g+1)\deg\mathcal L\geq2g+1$. (This is the choice made in the Lean proof `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isAmple_of_degree_pos_of_isAlgClosed`; the blueprint's "$m\gg0$".)

proof.text: $C$ is a proper smooth connected curve of genus $g$ over the algebraically closed field $k$ and $\mathcal M:=\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is a line bundle on $C$ (step 1) with $\deg\mathcal M\geq2g+1$ (step 2). By [lem-sc-degree-2g1-very-ample], applied to $\mathcal M$, the bundle $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is very ample.

source.place: ## Proof (the one paragraph); unit sk-thm-picard-rr, proof of (G), last sentence

proof.text: By [def-sc-ample], an invertible module is ample when some tensor power $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ with $m\geq1$ is very ample; step 3 gives this for $m=2g+1\geq1$. Hence $\mathcal L$ is ample.
